description: A list of concrete tasks, each ONE action in ONE place done by a community member from their own account: "post our launch in the FraCMO Slack #intros", "list us on this directory", "submit us to this newsletter". Use it when the user's buyers gather in specific communities, newsletters or directories, and a member posting there beats an ad. NOT for several people replying to, quoting or reposting ONE social post — that is boost_post (it takes space_id too); here every task needs its own place. Read productclank://guides/action-campaign first and plan the list WITH the user. TWO STEPS: (1) call without confirmed — a FREE dry run: every task is checked (duplicate places, places in the 14-day cooldown, open tasks in communities), and you get the publish price (credits per task) and the cash deposit for usdc tasks. Show the user the list, the warnings and the price. (2) On a yes, call again with confirmed:true: the campaign is created HELD (tasks are drafts, nothing is live, nothing charged). Then: usdc tasks → give the user fund_url to deposit; then publish_action_tasks (charges credits per task).

brief.description: What the campaign is for, shown to participants

confirmed.description: Leave unset for the free dry run. true ONLY after the user agreed to the list and the price.

space_id.description: Run inside one of the user's spaces (id from list_spaces; members only, Stars). Omit for the public network.

target_url.description: Where each task's tracked link sends people (the product / a landing page). Default: the product's website.

destination_url.description: Invite, channel or listing URL — identifies the place for the one-task-per-place rule

draft_text.description: A starting draft written for that place. Members rewrite it.

instructions.description: Where exactly, when, the place's rules

mode.description: Default exclusive. open ONLY for reviews / stars / sign-ups

reward_amount.description: Points, or dollars for usdc — an amount, never a percent

name: create_action_campaign
title: Create an action campaign (tasks: one action in one place)
